title: For Alas Women, winning one game is no easy task

blocks.text: The level of confidence seems very high, but can Alas Women Pilipinas translate it into success at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026? Can the Nationals match the historic fourth place finish of the previous national team in the 1962 edition? It’s hard to make an early assessment considering what has transpired in the association over the past few months. But one thing is sure, Bella Belen and other Alas members are doing everything humanly possible to make their stint in the continental showpiece worth remembering. In a recent PVL On Tour gig in Victorias City, Negros Occidental, Belen, who plays for Capital1 Solar Energy, claimed they are trying to work on all facets of their game – especially on the defensive end – under the watchful eyes of Japanese coach Taka Minowa, to be at par with some of the region’s best. Belen is one 12 luminaries in a constellation of volleyball stars carrying the hopes of the entire nation, joining 452 other members of the Team Philippines in this quadrennial extravaganza. Actually, the Nationals need only to win once in their three-country group elims to advance to the quarters. While that sounds easy, it is still difficult since the 58th-ranked Alas has to hurdle the dangerous Kazakhstan before scaling the perilous Great Wall that is China. The Kazakhstanis are no pushovers being ranked No. 41, while the Chinese are rated highly at No. 7, second best in the region next to host and No. 6 Japan. The situation is even more complicated for the men’s side. The Alas Men landed in a ‘Group of Death’ alongside China, South Korea and Chinese Taipei and must beat two of these opposition to qualify to the quarters. Given more time to prepare this time around– it is scheduled to leave for Japan early to undergo training camp – Gilas Women is ready to rip up the charts and make a lasting impression. Joining Belen on the star-studded team are fellow Capital1 standout Erika Santos, former NU teammate Alyssa Solomon, La Salle’s Angel Canino, Marionne Alba, Dawn Catindig, Julia de Guzman, Thea Gagate, Ylizyeth Jazareno, Eya Laure, Dell Palomata, and Amie Provido.
